item.title: Darian Mensah faces biggest test to date as Miami prepares for Notre Dame without Malachi Toney
item.description: Darian Mensah faces biggest test to date as Miami prepares for Notre Dame without Malachi Toney originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Miami Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah has emerged as one of college football's biggest stars, leading the nation in touchdown passes while helping the Hurricanes secure the No. 1 spot in the initial College Football Playoff rankings. But Saturday's showdown against the No. 4 Notre Dame Fighting Irish presents his biggest challenge yet. Mensah will take the field without his top receiver, Malachi Toney, who suffered an ankle injury during Wednesday's practice and underwent surgery. Toney, who led the nation with 73 receptions and 13 receiving touchdowns, is expected to return later this season. The significant loss for Miami's offense could have implications on Mensah's success. Despite the setback, Hurricanes coach Mario Cristobal gave a vote of confidence in Mensah's preparation and leadership. "He's eager to get the ball," Cristobal said this week. "Enthusiasm, excited, doesn't flinch, very focused. Just ready, prepared." Mensah has been outstanding this season, throwing for 25 touchdown passes while completing 80.7% of his attempts. Those numbers are unheard of in the modern era. That completion percentage would surpass the NCAA single-season record of 77.4%, set by Bo Nix in 2023. Miami also leads the nation in scoring, averaging 46.7 points per game. The former Duke quarterback's rise reflects the growing influence of the transfer portal and NIL opportunities in college football. At his third stop, which included Tulane, Mensah joined Miami and established himself as a Heisman Trophy contender. His estimated $6.5 million NIL valuation, according to On3 , is the highest in men's college athletics. His endorsement partners include Dr Pepper, CVS and Sling TV. Mensah has the important opportunity to impress NFL scouts against the Irish. Despite his impressive numbers, he has faced limited competition against ranked opponents. "I want to see you go up against a more high-profile team," The Athletic's Dane Brugler told Front Office Sports . Miami needs another significant victory to boost its playoff resume, while Notre Dame faces considerable pressure. After losing to BYU, the Fighting Irish can't suffer another loss this season. While they currently sit at No. 11 in the playoff rankings, this is a wide gap despite holding the No. 4 position in the AP Top 25. The game also carries Heisman implications. With Toney sidelined, Mensah has an opportunity to take a step forward in his candidacy for the nation's top award. For Miami, the challenge is clear to stay on top. Being able to maintain its offensive dominance without its most productive receiver will be tough. Mensah could be in the midst of his defining performance of his season. item.title: Kiwis reap rewards of gamble on 'freak of nature' Ponga
item.description: Kalyn Ponga helped Newcastle Knights reach October's NRL Grand Final [Getty Images] "He's a tough character and he was so adamant he was playing." Kalyn Ponga, in the words of his head coach Stacey Jones, was never going to miss New Zealand's Rugby League World Cup semi-final. But it was a remarkable return to action for a player whose tournament turned from dream to nightmare just over three weeks ago. In the World Cup opener against Australia in Sydney on 15 October, Ponga seemed to be enjoying a perfect New Zealand debut. Then it all went wrong. The 28-year-old scored two second-half tries but was forced off late in the game - having played for 20 minutes with a broken left forearm sustained in a tackle with Cameron Munster. The Kiwis went on to lose 24-22; Ponga required surgery. Just 23 days later, their talismanic full-back – initially named as a reserve, and then on the interchange bench – made a shock return to the starting 13 and delivered a starring performance as New Zealand overpowered Tonga 34-10 to reach their first Men's Rugby League World Cup final for 13 years. "Where sports science is these days – I saw what he had in his arm, the rod or plate was covering his whole arm," Jones said. "We didn't know until after our second-to-last training that he was going to be all right – he ticked all the boxes. Just a tough person." His fancy footwork and slick handling setting up scores for Briton Nikora, Casey McLean and Xavier Willison. He largely dominated the contest with opposite number Lehi Hopoate, notably clearing out the full-back as he fumbled a grubber kick in Tonga's in-goal area for New Zealand's second try, scored by Dane Gagai. In defence, a bruising try-saving block on Demitric Vaimauga indicated no cause for concern about his wounded wing. "Obviously a freak of a player," said Kiwis captain James Fisher-Harris. "The defensive mindset he had tonight, he saved a couple of tries. That's what I love about KP. "He's a freak of nature. His leadership skills are underrated. He's really good for us, our spine especially." But while it was undoubtedly the Ponga show at the home of his NRL side Newcastle Knights, New Zealand are not just a one-man band. item.title: Ice hockey chiefs mull all 'avenues' for German worlds as Russia waits
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Czech Republic's Dmitrij Jaskin (L) and Russia's Sergei Plotnikov battle for the puck during the 2019 IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship Bronze medal match ice hockey match between Russia and Czech Republic at the Ondrej Nepela Arena. (is associated with: «Ice hockey chiefs mull all 'avenues' for German worlds as Russia waits») Martti Kainulainen/Lehtikuva/dpa "All available avenues" are being considered by the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) as it tries to find a way forward after Russia was allowed to compete in the men's world championship in Germany in May. The decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) prompted dismay among other nations, sponsors and politicians. Several countries said they would boycott games against Russia at the championship given the ongoing war in Ukraine, while sponsors said they would think about withdrawing. Germany is mulling whether to hand back the hosting rights or not give visas to the Russian team. "While the IIHF continues to disagree with the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) concerning Russian participation in IIHF Championships, we are taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships," a statement said on Saturday. "The IIHF must work within the applicable framework while upholding its responsibility to preserve international competition and protect the sport as a whole. The IIHF is therefore exploring all available avenues." The federation also confirmed that Belarus, which has helped Russia in its war on Ukraine, remains banned from international ice hockey competition. The International Olympic Committee lifted a ban on the Russian Olympic Committee in July, but it is being left up to individual sporting bodies if and how Russia is reincorporated, despite the Ukraine war still raging after four years. The IIHF opted to continue to exclude Russian teams on security grounds, but Russia appealed to the world's top sports court and won. The ruling could have implications for other sports.

item.title: Mustangs get back to basics in state quarterfinal win over Wrightstown
item.description: Mark Krommenacker isn't above reproach when it comes to his play-calling. The second-year Little Chute head coach admitted that maybe he went a little too exotic in some of his calls in the second quarter of the Mustangs' WIAA Division 4 state football quarterfinal matchup Nov. 6 against Wrightstown. A pick-six in the second quarter gave the Tigers a halftime lead, but the Mustangs went back to basics in the second half to upend the Tigers 26-14. Little Chute (11-1) moves on to the state semifinals to face North Eastern Conference rival Freedom (12-0) at Ashwaubenon High School on Nov. 13. The Mustangs led 12-7 after the first quarter and were looking to stage another scoring drive when Wrightstown's Lincoln Hermsen picked off a play-action pass from Jaden Hermsen at the line of scrimmage and returned it 35 yards for the touchdown. That made the score 14-12 at the half and Krommenacker knew what he had to do in the second half. "We were a little bit maybe shell-shocked at that time, and rightfully so, because Wrightstown came out and had a good plan and got after us," Krommenacker said. "I think it's my fault. I got a little too fancy at times with some play calls and turns out you need to probably just pound it and get it to some of your best players and run behind some of your best players." That's exactly what the Mustangs did as they controlled the clock in the third quarter. Little Chute retook the lead 20-14 on Trevor Verhagen's 10-yard score. That 12-play, 62-yard drive began off a Reece Joten interception and Joten also put the offense on his shoulders on the scoring drive, rushing for 31 yards on eight carries, including seven consecutive. "We know that we're a very physical team and we just had to fix up some mental errors," Joten said. "And once those mental errors were out, we just did our assignment and then we could just push the ball." item.title: Isaiah Marshall keeps progressing toward starting for Kansas football
item.description: LAWRENCE — Isaiah Marshall continues to look more and more likely of being able to start at quarterback Saturday for Kansas football, at home against UCF. Marshall, a redshirt sophomore and the team's regular starter this fall at the position, didn’t play in last week’s game at TCU as he dealt with what coach Lance Leipold would describe as a lower-leg issue. When the Big 12 Conference’s player availability reports started to come out on Wednesday this week, Marshall was listed as questionable — as were redshirt junior quarterbacks Cole Ballard and Chase Jenkins. But like Jenkins, Marshall was listed as probable on Thursday, and on Friday neither of those two were listed at all. RELATED: How to watch Kansas football vs UCF, including time, TV, streaming Ballard, of course, does remain questionable for Kansas ’ game against UCF. Ballard stepped in as the starter during last week’s loss against TCU. But having Marshall and Jenkins available would provide KU with a pair of players with starting experience, Marshall from this season with the Jayhawks and Jenkins from his time at Rice earlier in his college career. Kansas’ game against UCF is set to kick off at 2:45 p.m. (CT) in Lawerence. The Jayhawks (3-5, 1-4 in Big 12) are looking to bounce back this weekend, as they look to continue to position themselves for a bowl game this fall. item.title: Jacob Warren returning to old form in return from injury for Mason football
item.description: MASON — Jacob Warren had hopes of contributing as a running back or linebacker this fall for the Mason football team as it chased its goals. But those hopes took an early hit when Warren broke his left ankle during a four-way scrimmage in August. The break wasn't severe enough where Warren held out hope he could potentially return to the field this season. And that opportunity has come in the MHSAA playoffs. Warren has scored touchdowns the last two weeks while helping Mason capture a fifth district title in six years. That included having four carries for 59 yards and a TD in a 49-0 win over Fenton in a Division 3 district final Friday, Nov. 6. "I'm really lucky my injury was the best it could have been for the situation," Warren said. "I'm just so blessed to be able to be back on the field. "I'm so lucky to have the support system I have around me and the family, friends and coaches that supported me all the 10 weeks I was out. It's so awesome to be back on the football field." Warren has 10 carries for 110 yards and the two TDs the last two weeks. Mason coach Gary Houghton sensed Warren was getting back to his old form in recent practices and said his presence gives the Bulldogs another threat in the backfield to complement Troy Peters and Jeffrey Reisner, who each rushed for more than 100 yards Friday. "He's just a very dynamic athlete, a very smart football player and he's patient," Houghton said. "He'll let his blocks develop and he'll accelerate and go. He's just one of the quickest kids I've ever coached and just a really dynamic kid in space." Warren was cleared for a return a few weeks ago and is ready to do whatever is needed to help the Bulldogs try to extend their playoff run a few more weeks. The next step on the journey for Mason is a trip next week to Chelsea, which is where Warren suffered his injury. "I'm stoked," Warren said. "Obviously it sucked in the scrimmage the week before the first game (to get hurt). I'm just so excited to maybe get a little redemption next week. I can't wait." item.title: Tottenham dealt latest attacking injury blow after VAR madness at Leeds
item.description: Tottenham have been dealt another attacking injury blow after Mathys Tel limped off before half-time against Leeds . Tel was unable to continue after being on the end of a stamp by Jayden Bogle, who caught the Frenchman on the ankle with his studs. VAR spent over four minutes reviewing the incident to determine whether it was a red card offence, only for referee John Brooks - who didn’t even caution Bogle initially - to be told to stick with the on-field decision. This meant the right wing-back got away with the challenge scot free. “The referee’s call of no red card to Bogle for the challenge on Tel was checked and confirmed by VAR,” said the Premier League Match Centre. Should Jason Bogle have seen red for this challenge? 🟥👀 📺 Stream live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/fuK42Okkcz — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 7, 2026 The statement added VAR Tony Harrington’s verdict to Brooks: “I'm confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There’s a lack of speed going into the challenge and he’s stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge”. The challenge was similar to the one that saw Jean-Philippe Mateta shown red after a VAR review when Spurs played Crystal Palace last weekend. Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi was visibly frustrated with the outcome of the review and his woes were exacerbated when Tel signalled to the bench that he would need to come off, having tried to play through the pain for five minutes. Tel was replaced by Dominic Solanke in the 43rd minute, who was dropped from the starting line-up following the Palace win. Mathys Tel was forced off during Tottenham's clash with Leeds (Getty) De Zerbi’s attacking options have already been ravaged by injury this season and the club will now be left to sweat over the extent of Tel’s setback. Savio and Mykhailo Mudryk are out until after the international break, while Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert are continuing to work their way back from serious knee injuries, with both eyeing returns after the turn of the year. Tel has impressed for Spurs in recent weeks, scoring a stunning solo goal in their 2-0 win over Chelsea on 24 October, the club’s first victory at Stamford Bridge since 2018.

item.title: Report: Bills are looking to trade for a defensive back
item.description: This is not exactly a shock, but now we have a report from a national insider about what the Buffalo Bills are looking for at the NFL trade deadline. That insider is Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer. I recently tweeted the lack of reports this season represents a stark contrast to recent years, when the Bills were listed in essentially every trade-deadline insight article in the weeks leading up to the deadline. Now, there was one mention of the Bills’ intentions, from Breer, in late October. We wrote about here at Rumblings. It was one sentence and relatively vague compared to the rest of the mentions pertaining to other teams and trade chips. “ The Bills are looking for another piece or two on defense .” This time around, in a response to a tweet that highlighted the lack of a Bills mention in his latest trade-deadline article , Breer wrote this: I had it in my last trade column, and will add it here—The Bills are still looking in to adding a piece on the defensive side of the ball. And specifically at corner and safety. https://t.co/CkjvAiQRLa — Albert Breer (@AlbertBreer) November 7, 2026 The positions are the unexpected part. However, the Bills have recently added Tre’Davious White and Kader Kohou to the practice squad at cornerback. They just got a quality effort from Te’Cory Couch in the slot. At safety, Jordan Hancock is close to returning. Damar Hamlin is playing sound football. Geno Stone tied for the team lead in tackles with six against the Ravens on just 19 snaps, and he tipped a pass that led to Davison Igbinosun’s first career interception. According to Breer, the Bills are want to add a defensive back at the trade deadline. We’ll see if it happens.

The Philadelphia Eagles are turning to Joe Milton as their new starting quarterback in Week 9 against the New York Giants, replacing Tanner McKee. Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni had said McKee would be the starter earlier in the week, but he later changed his mind and went with Milton. Sirianni addressed the media about his QB U-turn, which he claims was a strategic move to try and unsettle the Giants. “I’m gonna tell you what I want to tell you, guys. item.title: Patriots inducting Rob Gronkowski into team’s Hall of Fame
item.description: FOXBORO, MA - SEPTEMBER 10: Rob Gronkowski #87 of the New England Patriots celebrates after a touchdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Gillette Stadium on September 10, 2015 in Foxboro, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Maddie Meyer Legendary New England Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski will be inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame Saturday. Gronkowski beat out fellow Patriots legends Adam Vinatieri and Logan Mankins in a fan vote to become the 38th inductee. Gronk spent 9 seasons in New England after being drafted in the second round of the 2010 NFL Draft. The Patriots won the AFC East in each of Gronk’s seasons and made the Super Bowl 5 times, hoisting three Lombardi’s. Gronkowski ranks first in Patriots history with 80 total touchdowns (79 receiving and one rushing), and his 7,861 receiving yards are second in team history. Gronk’s connection with QB Tom Brady was often unstoppable on the field during their time in New England. The two went to go on to play for the Buccaneers before Gronk retired in March of 2019. Gronk’s ceremony comes the same weekend Brady is expected to call the Patriots vs. Packers game at Gillette Sunday afternoon as a broadcaster for the first time. item.description: Real Madrid 17-year-old academy talent earns comparisons to Bernardo Silva Real Madrid midfielder Marco Company is making significant progress at Valdebebas, establishing himself as one of the standout performers in the club’s Juvenil A side, earning him comparisons with Bernardo Silva within the club, reports AS . After arriving from Valencia in 2023, the 17-year-old talent has taken an important step in his development this season, combining regular involvement with an impressive contribution in front of goal. Notably, his emergence comes at an important moment for Real Madrid’s youth team, who have made an excellent start to their domestic and European campaigns. Company establishes himself as a key player at Real Madrid Company made his debut for Juvenil A last season, but it is the current campaign that has seen him become a much more influential figure. To put it in perspective, he is now the second-most-used midfielder in the squad behind Cherif Fofana. Statistically, Company is performing at an excellent level, scoring three goals and providing five assists across 485 minutes in La Liga and the UEFA Youth League. Marco Company is making waves at Real Madrid’s youth team. (Picture credit: Instagrtam/@marcocompany) His performances have helped Juvenil A maintain their strong start to the season. They have won all four of their UEFA Youth League group-stage matches and collected seven victories and one draw from eight league fixtures. Qualities that have caught attention at Valdebebas Company’s ability to influence attacking situations from midfield is one of the characteristics that has made him an exciting prospect. When he was younger, he was frequently compared to Mikel Merino because of his movement into the penalty area and ability to arrive in scoring positions. However, the assessment of his potential at Valdebebas has evolved, and those following his development now see similarities with Vitinha and Bernardo Silva, particularly in terms of his playing style and technical qualities. item.description: England have been dealt a hammer blow to their seam bowling department for the upcoming tour of Australia as Josh Tongue will miss the trip down under due to a toe injury. Tongue made his One Day International (ODI) debut earlier this year in a contest against India in Birmingham. He took 1-50 from his 10 overs and has since been selected in four other one day games. His most recent outing was against Sri Lanka in the ODI Tri-Series which also included Pakistan. Tongue took 3-79 from 8.5 overs as the Sri Lankans made history by knocking off 429 runs with one ball remaining in the game. item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship bursts back into life as the inaugural edition comes to a conclusion in a busy November. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action. France and South Africa currently top the two pools, with New Zealand also unbeaten and level on points with the Springboks. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how it will all work: What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. The 1st vs 1st match is worth two points, with all other matches in the finals weekend worth one. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom will be able to watch every game on ITV after the free-to-air broadcaster struck a deal to show the competition. item.description: Thomas Tuchel tells England fans to stop booing Ben White Ben White could face another hostile reception from England supporters during the November international break, despite returning to the national team under Thomas Tuchel. The Arsenal defender has previously been booed by sections of the crowd because of his decision to step away from international football. The situation stems from his earlier disagreement with a member of Gareth Southgate’s coaching staff, which led to his absence from the England setup. White remained away from the national team until Tuchel took charge, with the new manager showing confidence in his ability and welcoming him back into the squad. The defender is now one of five Arsenal players selected for England’s latest fixtures and will be hoping to make a positive impression. Tuchel has shown that he trusts White, making it likely that he will receive an opportunity to play during the international break. Tuchel wants England fans to move on However, there is no guarantee that supporters will change their attitude towards White immediately. The defender could still face boos if he features in either of England’s two matches, something Tuchel believes should no longer happen. The England manager has acknowledged that fans were disappointed by the circumstances surrounding White’s previous departure. Nevertheless, he believes the defender has already demonstrated his commitment and quality since returning to the international setup. Tuchel wants the situation to become a closed chapter, allowing White to concentrate on representing his country without having to deal with hostility from the stands. England manager backs Arsenal defender Speaking via the Metro , Tuchel explained why he believes White deserves the support of England supporters and highlighted the positive impression he made during his previous camp. ‘We could understand the disappointment of the fans with what happened before but I think this is expressed now and this should be a closed book because I think everyone could also see the investment of Ben, the quality of Ben and how he presented himself in the March camp before the World Cup. ‘He did excellent, scored for us and then I think he committed a foul and we conceded.
